newsitem.title: UK: Singer Dana ready to stand for Irish presidency.
newsitem.headline: Singer Dana ready to stand for Irish presidency.

text.p: Dana, a popular Irish singer and devout Roman Catholic, said on Wednesday she was willing to run for the job of Irish president.
Mary Robinson is stepping down as president to become United Nations Human Rights Commissioner and Dana, a leading anti-abortion crusader, said she would like to challenge for the post.

Dana, whose real name is Rosemary Brown, has been put forward by the pro-life lobby. Her singing career took off in 1970 when she won the Eurovision Song Contest, an international pop festival, with a ballad called "All Kinds of Everything".
Speaking from her home in Birmingham, Alabama, Dana said she had discussed with her husband and children the possibility of standing for the job.
"With their support, if I was nominated, I would be willing to give up my career and be a candidate for the presidency," she told BBC Radio in an interview.
But she pledged not to push her own strong personal beliefs in the crusade to become titular head of Ireland in the figurehead post.

Dana said Robinson "promised going into the role that as president she would uphold the constitution and that her own personal beliefs would not interfere with that, and I would make the same pledge".
But Dana, 45, needs the support of 20 Irish members of parliament to secure a nomination. She did not know if she could get the required backing.
"If I were lucky enough to be elected as president,the first thing I should like to look at is how the president is elected.

"It's supposed to be an open process and should be the direct choice of the people. But at present you must have the support of a party before you can go forward, and a lot of people within the island think that this should be changed."
If he decides to run, moderate Irish nationalist John Hume, one of the architects of the Northern Ireland peace process, is considered to be hot favourite to replace Robinson.
